data.gender_notes: Angle is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Angle was the goddess of the bend or curve. She was also associated with the turning of the seasons and the changing of the year. The name Angle comes from the Old English word ‘engel’, which means ‘messenger’ or ‘angel’. In Christianity, Angels are celestial beings who serve as messengers of God. The name Angle carries the meaning “Turner, Bender” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Angle usually hope their child will grow to embody turner, bender and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Angle total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.
